BuyerActionGrant.description: The single-use grant from `/portal/action-codes/verify`. Required on a code session; ignored for a `portal:write` merchant token.
BuyerActionGrant.name: X-Buyer-Action-Grant

FacadeChannel.description: Where the approval came from. Recorded with it. Default `api`.
FacadeChannel.name: X-Infi-Channel

FacadeCursor.description: Opaque cursor from the previous page's `nextCursor`.
FacadeCursor.name: cursor

FacadeDraftKey.description: A UUID the caller chooses. Saving again with it recovers a lost response.
FacadeDraftKey.name: draftKey

FacadeHash.description: The `draftHash` you hold. A different current hash answers 412.
FacadeHash.name: hash

FacadeIfMatch.description: The `draftHash` you reviewed, quoted. Absent answers 428.
FacadeIfMatch.name: If-Match

FacadeIfMatchOptional.description: The `draftHash` you reviewed, quoted. Absent only creates.
FacadeIfMatchOptional.name: If-Match

FacadePlanHash.description: The `planHash` of the plan you reviewed, quoted. Absent answers 428.
FacadePlanHash.name: If-Match

IdempotencyKey.description: Client-supplied key for safe retries. The first response for a key is stored and replayed verbatim on any retry with the same key.
IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key

LegacyEnrollmentID.description:
Product enrollment UUID (product_customers.id). Legacy SDK paths use this
parameter name; subscriptions, invoices, and credit wallets reference enrollment IDs.
LegacyEnrollmentID.name: customerID

LinkID.description: Payment link UUID. Revoke resolves the link by tenant + linkID only — the `productID` in the path is not used to scope it.
LinkID.name: linkID

LinkToken.description: The payment link's opaque `plink_*` token. This IS the capability — holding it is the whole authorization, which is why these routes take no API key.
LinkToken.name: token

Conflict.description: Conflicting state. Two shapes: a handler conflict (ConflictError) or the Idempotency-Key replay guard, which is written by middleware and uses the nested envelope (MiddlewareError, `code: idempotency_key_reused`).

DraftChanged.description: The draft is not the one you hold. Nothing was saved or published. `current` is the draft as it is now, null when it does not exist.

Forbidden.description: Authenticated but not allowed (e.g. no tenant membership)

IfMatchRequired.description: Publishing needs `If-Match` with the draft hash you reviewed.

PlanChanged.description: The account is not the one the plan was computed against. Nothing was applied. `current` is the plan as it computes now (null if it cannot be computed); review it and apply that one.

PortalChallenge.description: A challenge was opened (a code is mailed only to a known address)

RateLimited.description: Rate limit exceeded. Uses the nested middleware envelope, not the flat one. `Retry-After` gives the wait in seconds.

ServiceUnavailable.description: A required dependency (e.g. object storage) is not configured

Statement.description: The statement as a download (`Content-Disposition: attachment`, never cached).

ValidationFailed.description: One or more fields are invalid. The per-field detail is in `errors[]`; read it, the top-level `message` is often generic.

id.description: Public id with its prefix (conv_, msg_, run_, draft_, ADR 0015); a bare UUID is still accepted on input.
Public id with its prefix (conv_, msg_, run_, draft_, ADR 0015); a bare UUID is still accepted on input.

title.description: Start of the first message the caller sent; empty before the first message.

capability.description: Browser-only capability returned once. Never put in model context, ordinary telemetry or URL query parameters.

id.description: Public id with its prefix (conv_, msg_, run_, draft_, ADR 0015); a bare UUID is still accepted on input.
Public id with its prefix (conv_, msg_, run_, draft_, ADR 0015); a bare UUID is still accepted on input.

blocked.description: For a plan part, whether the plan has a change that cannot be applied.

items.description: For a plan part, each product the plan touches, for the confirmation card.

price.description: Base price of the version to be published, decimal in major units.

staying.description: Subscribers who keep paying the version they agreed to.

lines.description: For a plan part, the changes that are not products (meters, webhooks), as the plan's own sentences.

state.description: Actual command operation state, independent of assistant run completion.

id.description: Public id with its prefix (conv_, msg_, run_, draft_, ADR 0015); a bare UUID is still accepted on input.

operations.description: Persisted command outcomes, including results admitted before run cancellation.

AccountId.description: A business's (tenant's) id. Starts with `acct_`; the rest is 22 base62 characters. A bare UUID is still accepted as input while clients move over.

offset.description: The part of owed the Account's debt paid.

status.description: offset means the Account's debt paid the whole cycle and nothing was sent.

transfer.description: owed − offset: what goes through Wise, before any conversion.

amount.description: Signed; a negative row lowers the debt.
What the payout took of the debt

convertedAmount.description: What the debt paid of the payout, in payoutCurrency, at Wise's mid-market rate with no spread.

payoutCurrency.description: Set when the debt was in another currency than the payout (ADR 0023, amended 2026-10-16).

state.description: reserved while the payout waits, settled once paid, released when it ended without paying.

source.description: What made the debt: refund_reversal (a refund of a sale already paid out), refund_fee (Stripe's fee on a refund, ADR 0023), payout_excess (a refund that landed while the payout was in flight), payout_returned (a returned payout giving that back), dispute, dispute_fee, dispute_won, dispute_processor_fee (Stripe's fee on a disputed share, ADR 0020) and dispute_processor_fee_won (its return when the dispute is won), reserve_applied (a held reserve a debt took first, ADR 0027) and reserve_released (a reserve whose day came, a credit the cycle pays).

AccountReceivables.description: What the Account owes the UK Ltd and how payouts took it back.

balances.description: Open debt per currency; only currencies with a balance.

AccountReserves.description: What the UK Ltd holds back of the Account's payouts under its reserve tier (ADR 0027). It is still the Account's money, not a fee: it is released in the first cycle after its day, or a debt takes it first.

balances.description: Held per currency; only currencies with something held.

releases.description: What is released on each day, per currency, oldest first.

name.description: Label of a CLI project key (create-infi-app · loja · mac); absent for keys made in the dashboard.

fromState.description: Absent with current audit producers, which do not persist the previous state.

toState.description: Recognized persisted state or configuration status. It does not imply financial confirmation.

route.description: Normalized route template without parameter values or query strings.

ApiKeyUsage.description: Exact aggregates over retained captured observations in [from, to). Request count includes all HTTP statuses; errors are status >= 400. Error rate is errorCount/requestCount between 0 and 1, or zero when empty. Average is the arithmetic mean and p95 uses continuous percentile interpolation. Empty latency aggregates are zero. Last use is the latest retained captured request before to, including refusals, and may precede the selected window. It is null when no retained observation exists, not proof the key was never used. Capture can lose observations under overload; these are not billing-grade totals.

Appearance.description: A buyer page's resolved look — values only. Resolved link → product → business → default (docs/product-specs/templates/dashboard-v1-api.md).

autoChargeEnabled.description: Whether invoices may be collected from a stored credential with nobody present. Defaults to false, per tenant, deliberately.

cardAutoChargeAvailable.description: Whether a stored card could be charged off-session at all here. No provider does it until Unit 6 (the UK Ltd's off-session charge), so this is false — and autoChargeEnabled would be a switch with nothing to charge.

topupDailyCap.description: Decimal string. Per payer per day, across top-up policies.

BusinessAppearance.description: The business theme every product and link inherits. On a write, an absent field is left alone and "" clears it (back to the default).

projectId.description: The CLI's stable id for this project.

reused.description: The project already held this key; no secret is returned.

secret.description: Only when the key was minted by this call.

apiKey.description: The welcome key, minted only on the sandbox deployment (an sk_test_ key). Absent on live: a live account starts unactivated and gets no credentials until Go Live — see ADR 0057.

inputSchema.description: JSON Schema of the `input` the action takes.

actionId.description: The `id` of an action the snapshot offered.

publicKey.description: Public Core v5 tokenization key; returned only after preparation succeeds.

preparation.description: Opaque capability sent in a POST body for token-free readback.
Opaque short-lived preparation capability; never a card token.

token.description: Transient one-use Core v5 token. Never stored or included in telemetry.

CheckoutChargeRequest.description: `method` is validated server-side and answers **422** (not 400) when missing, outside the enum, or not offered in the checkout's `paymentOptions`. The current UK integration offers only `card`. A request for `pix` is refused rather than converted to card, before creating an Order, updating payer tax ID, or preparing a payment.

autoTopup.description: The buyer of a credit package ticked "automatic top-up" (offered when `autoTopupAvailable`): the card is saved on the UK account under the mandate the charge returns, and the merchant's policy can then buy the package again with nobody present. Send it only when ticked; ignored on an offer that is not a credit package.

remember.description: Payer ticked "lembrar de mim": asks Infi to remember them as a person across stores. Never an authorization to charge a card. Send it only when ticked.

rememberTextVersion.description: The wording the payer saw — echo `remember.version` from the checkout read. What the server records as the version accepted.

surface.description: `embed` when the page paying is inside a merchant's iframe. On a UK Ltd sale it makes a redirect-based method return to the embed's own Order page (`/pay` refuses to be framed). Omit on `/pay`. Infi builds the return URL; the browser never supplies one.

withdrawalWaiver.description: The buyer ticked the page's `withdrawalWaiver`: they ask for the digital content at once and acknowledge that it ends the statutory right of withdrawal (plan 6f). Required on every UK sale but the payment of a renewal: without it the charge answers 422 `withdrawal_waiver_required` before anything is frozen or sent to Stripe. The Order records the version, the words and the IP, and the receipt e-mail repeats them.

CheckoutInteractionSnapshot.description: A checkout session as the agent contract reads it, at its public level (no contact: the session id travels in a URL, so it reaches referrers and logs). The browser reads the same document as an agent on purpose, so a page and an API never disagree about whether someone paid.

actions.description: What the buyer may do next. Null when there is nothing to do (a charge in flight, a paid session).

codeChallenge.description: Appears once a purchase code was sent. Never the code, nor the full destination.

consentDigest.description: Over what the buyer agrees to (who is paid, how much, in what currency, for what). Echo it on an action; a changed bargain is 409 `consent_changed`.

humanUrl.description: The hosted page for the same link.

nextPollAfterMs.description: How long to wait before reading again while a payment is in flight.

payment.description: The public card payment projection, when the Session-owned attempt is linked. Lets a reload resume after a lost submit response.

purchaseId.description: The invoice, once the first charge materialized it.

requiredFields.description: What the session still needs before a charge can be attempted.

revision.description: Moves with every state change. Echo it on an action; a stale one is 409 `stale_revision`.

status.description: `payment_unknown` is a charge the provider never answered: keep asking, never charge again.

unavailableReason.description: Why this purchase cannot currently accept payment.

CheckoutMandate.description: Present when this payment saves the buyer's card on Infi's UK company's Stripe account for later charges with nobody present (renewals, automatic top-ups, purchases the buyer confirms). Show `text` verbatim next to the pay button: paying under it is the buyer's acceptance, and the payment records `version`. Stripe's own reuse notice is hidden, so this is the only authorization on the page.

version.description: Echo it as `consentTextVersion` on the charge.

logoUrl.description: Absent when the merchant has no logo. Absolute, immutable per upload.

CheckoutRememberOffer.description: The "lembrar de mim" wording, rendered by the server so the version a buyer accepts names words they actually read.

version.description: Echo it as `rememberTextVersion` on the charge.

acceptsPayments.description: False when the store cannot receive a payment yet (the UK Ltd has not admitted it): `paymentOptions` is then empty and the checkout says so instead of offering a method. Never omitted.

autoTopupAvailable.description: True when the offer is a credit package (a one-off sale whose product grants credits when paid) and the UK Ltd collects it: the page may offer "automatic top-up", and the charge then takes `autoTopup: true` to save the card under the mandate. Always present.

cardEnabled.description: Compatibility projection derived from paymentOptions. Always present.

mandate.description: Card-on-file authorization the payer must accept. Present only when card is available and the invoice is still open. `version` is what the client must echo as `consentTextVersion` when charging with `saveInstrument`.

logoUrl.description: Absent when the merchant has no logo. Absolute, on this API's host (`/pay/{slug}/logo/{file}`), immutable per upload.

paymentMethod.description: Method of the confirmed payment. Present only once the invoice is paid (it drives the shared receipt); absent otherwise.

unavailableReason.description: Why this purchase cannot currently accept payment. Missing buyer country allows collecting contact first. Domestic BR card/Pix remains unavailable until Pagar.me dispatch is integrated, without UK fallback. Supplier country can also be missing/conflicting, or the product may still require UK approval (ADR 0026).

CheckoutSessionAction.description: How the buyer pays an Order sold by Infi's UK company as merchant of record (ADR 0018, amended 2026-10-16): a Stripe Checkout Session in elements mode, mounted on the Order's own page (also inside the embed). Present only on the create-charge response of such an Order, and on a repeat of it while the session is open (the same session comes back). Load Stripe.js with `publishableKey`, mount Elements on `clientSecret` and confirm with `redirect: "if_required"`: a card, 3DS included, stays on the page. Then read the payment's status back; only the provider's webhook confirms it. A redirect-based method returns to the Order's page; never trust its query string. The client secret is transient: not stored, not on later reads.

mode.description: `setup` when nothing is charged now and the session only saves the card under `mandate` (a subscription whose first period is free): show no total and a "save card" action. Absent means `payment`.

CheckoutTotals.description: Totals of a UK Ltd sale. Prices include tax (ADR 0021): `total` is what the buyer pays, before and after payment. `provisional` before payment: Stripe Tax finds the tax inside the price on the hosted page, from the buyer's location, so `tax` is null and `subtotal` equals `total`. `final` once paid: `subtotal` is the sale excluding tax and `tax` the part of the total that was tax.

buyerCountry.description: Purchase country for direct collection or country established by Stripe Tax for final UK totals.

subtotal.description: The sale excluding tax once final; the tax-inclusive price while provisional.

ClaimTenantRequest.description: The claim flow's naming step. Both fields are optional and independent: a name alone derives the slug from it, a slug alone leaves the name as provisioned, neither leaves both alone.

accountName.description: Display name for the account, replacing `New app`.

slug.description: Lowercase alphanumeric words separated by single hyphens. Derived from `accountName` when omitted. Unique across the deployment — a slug already in use answers 409.

onboardingStep.description: Same vocabulary as session sync, and the two must agree. A claimed tenant is named, so this is `complete`. Untyped until now, which is how it went on emitting `integrate` after that step was deleted.

expiresAt.description: When an unclaimed tenant is reclaimed and its `sk_test_` key revoked. 30 days out: claiming means signing in, which means leaving the editor, which is the one thing this door promises the developer they will not have to do — so the window has to outlive an absence (ADR 0056). The welcome email includes this deadline (ADR 0059).

productId.description: The seeded "App usage" product. Provisioned unsellable on purpose — draft version 1, no key, no price — so publish a version and add a price before selling against it.

publishableKey.description:
An Infi `pk_test_` key, returned and RESERVED: **no route accepts it today.** Secret-key authentication rejects the `pk_` prefix outright, and nothing is mounted that takes one, so it authorizes nothing anywhere in this API. Never a payment-provider key.
The embedded checkout needs no key at all — the `plink_` payment-link token is the capability. Do not build against this field yet.

externalId.description: Telegram chat id or Discord guild id.

kind.description: api_key = an agent, the CLI or the MCP; session = a person.

approvalUrl.description: On live: where a person approves the proposal. It carries `?mode=live`, so the dashboard opens on the deployment the revision lives on.

secrets.description: Signing secrets of the endpoints this apply created, shown once.

from.description: The key a renamed product had.

key.description: Identity: product key, productKey/meterKey, or URL.

ref.description: How the SDK names it: product name, name/meter, or URL.

CompanyConfigOptions.description: Part of the plan's hash; apply must send the same.

adoptUnmanaged.description: Take over resources the document names that no revision wrote.

archiveOrphaned.description: Archive managed resources the document no longer names. Nothing is deleted.

overwriteDrift.description: Let the document win over edits made outside it.

blocked.description: A change waits on a decision; apply refuses a blocked plan.

signature.description: base64 Ed25519 over infi-config-promotion/v1, docHash, slug, sourceRevisionId, issuedAt (RFC 3339), newline-separated

CompanyDecimal.description: A decimal number as a string; money is never a float.

CompanyDocument.description: Company as code (ADR 0025): the catalog and webhooks a tenant declares. POST /config/plan diffs it against the tenant; POST /config/apply applies the plan. Keys are identity: a product by key, a meter by key within its product, a webhook by URL. Money, identity, payout setup and secrets never go here.

key.description: The slug track() sends. Immutable: renaming it would stop ingestion.

meter.description: Key of one of this product's meters. A flat amount is the product's basePrice, not a price.

basePrice.description: The recurring or flat fee. Zero, or at least the minimum charge.

billingCycle.description: Required for subscription and prepaid, refused otherwise.

description.description: Shown on the product page and the checkout.

guaranteeDays.description: Refund window: a buyer's refund asked inside it is automatic. Default 7.

key.description: Stable natural key, unique per tenant. Also the name when no name is given.

renamedFrom.description: The key this product had before. A rename is explicit, never a delete and a create.

events.description: Event types. Not limited to a list: delivery matches by name.

url.description: Identity of the endpoint. Its signing secret is minted by the server and shown once.

ConflictError.description: 409 body from a handler — Error plus `resource` and `metadata`.

metadata.description: Structured conflict context. `null` when the exception carried none.

ConsumptionRate.description: How usage of one meter becomes a wallet debit: quantity x factor, in units, with no rating and no currency. Flat by design — a tiered rate would make the debit non-incremental.

drawsFrom.description: The meter whose balance this one spends. OMIT IT for the common case: absent means the meter draws its own balance, which is what "10 images included per month" is. Set it only for a shared pool, where several meters spend one balance at different factors. A meter cannot draw its own balance explicitly (ADR 0054).

factor.description: Wallet units drawn per metered unit: a positive decimal string with at most 8 decimal places. 1 means the meter draws its own wallet one for one.

Coupon.description: A merchant discount applied to subscription invoices for a Stripe-style duration. `percentOff` is a decimal string.

CouponId.description: A coupon's id. Starts with `coup_`; the rest is 22 base62 characters. A bare UUID is still accepted as input while clients move over.

CreateCouponRequest.description: Create a coupon. Code matches `^[A-Z0-9_-]{3,32}$`; `percentOff` is a decimal string in (0, 100]. `durationInCycles` is required (>=1) for `repeating` and must be omitted otherwise.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (`BR`, `US`), normalized to upper case.

phone.description: Optional contact, normalized to E.164 digits by the existing identity rules. Does not identify a person or create a remote payment customer.

draft.description: Keep it an editor draft (no number, no event, not sent). `lineItems` is required otherwise.

send.description: Emit invoice.sent (email the payer) after finalize.

successUrl.description: Hosted checkout returns here after payment.

aggregation.description: `sum` bills the sum of each event's `value` (a missing value counts as 1); `count` bills the number of events, whatever `value` they carry. `unique_count`, `max` and `last` are refused with 422 `meter_aggregation_unsupported`.

valueProperty.description: Optional and stored as given; billing does not read it.

CreatePaymentLinkRequest.description: Optional. A link needs no configuration; send a body only to set where the payer goes afterwards. Both URLs must be absolute http(s).

productVersionId.description:
Sell a specific published version instead of the product's default. This is how a promotional price reaches a buyer: the version is published but not default, so nothing resolves into it by accident and only a link that names it can sell it.

Omit for the default version, which is what an ordinary link sells. Refused if the version is not a published version of this product.

amount.description: Override; defaults to the product's published base price.

externalId.description: Stable customer id (e.g. email); enroll is idempotent on it.

description.description: Line description; defaults to the product name.

accentColor.description: This product's own accent, over the business theme (link > product > business). "" clears it on a write; null inherits.

faq.description: Absent leaves the FAQ; an empty list clears it.

guaranteeDays.description: Refund window: a buyer's refund asked from the portal inside it is automatic; after it, the store decides. 7 (the CDC floor) when absent.

key.description: Stable per-tenant natural key. Creating twice with the same key returns the same product rather than failing; pricing that differs from its current version is refused with 422 (`pricing_immutable`).

media.description: Absent leaves the media; an empty list clears them.

postPurchaseRedirectUrl.description: Absolute http(s) URL the buyer lands on after paying. A link's own successUrl wins over it. "" clears it.

purchaseButtonText.description: The buy button's words. "" goes back to the element's default.

secret.description: The raw secret, returned only once at creation.
HMAC signing secret, returned only once at creation.

debt.description: What the creator owes the UK Ltd per currency; negative when the UK Ltd owes it.

winRate.description: Won over decided disputes, null with none decided.

reasons.description: Every rule that fired, with the value and the threshold it crossed.

Customer.description: Tenant-level end payer (unique externalId per tenant).

conversionPaymentId.description: Causal confirmed payment, preserved after refunds and cancellation.

convertedAt.description: Earliest evidenced dated confirmation time in system processing time. Null for leads and historical conversions with no reliable timestamp.

phone.description: Contact phone (E.164 digits, no leading `+`). Data for reaching, finding or weighing the buyer (dunning, LGPD) — never an identifier: a phone typed into a public checkout proves nothing about who typed it, so nothing resolves an identity from it.

CustomerConvertedData.description: Body of customer.converted. A confirmed payment converted this tenant customer. Emitted once on the lead-to-converted transition in the same transaction. Refunds and cancellation do not demote the customer. A merge may carry a historical conversion whose exact time is unknown.

externalId.description: Your own user id for this customer.

CustomerId.description: A customer's id. Starts with `cus_`; the rest is 22 base62 characters. A bare UUID is still accepted as input while clients move over.

nextCursor.description: Cursor of the next page; null on a short page.

CustomerState.description:
Single-read customer view: the enrollment, every balance it holds, live subscriptions, and current-period usage.
BREAKING (ADR 0054): `credit` is replaced by `balances`. It reported one hardcoded pool, and there is no default balance any more — a balance belongs to a declared meter, so the response names each one.

access.description: What the customer holds at the store: each product paid for and not fully refunded or charged back (`purchase`), and each subscription still running (`subscription`: active, trialing or past_due). The same list as `access` in `GET /v1/customer-sessions/verify`, for a server that knows the customer id and holds no buyer token.

balances.description: Every balance the enrollment holds, read the way the consumption gate reads it (the last checkpoint plus the entries after it), with the gate's verdict on each in `allowed`.

allowed.description: The consumption gate's rule applied to this balance: true when the product version has no floor for it or the balance is above that floor. A customer the gate has just blocked reads false here.

downloadUrl.description: Buyer-facing download link. Answers 410 once revokedAt is set.

emailSentAt.description: When the fulfillment email carrying this link went out.

revokedAt.description: When the download was turned off, set by a full refund or a chargeback on the payment behind it. Non-null means downloadUrl now answers 410 — stop rendering the button. Revoked grants are returned rather than hidden, because a grant that silently vanished would look like fulfillment never ran.

token.description: The bearer capability inside downloadUrl. Treat it like a password: anyone holding it downloads the paid product with no further proof of purchase.

Error.description: The standard error body for anything a handler raises. Flat — there is no `error` wrapper — and the correlation id is `tracer_id`, not `request_id`.

message.description: Customer-safe sentence. Never contains internal detail.

tracer_id.description: Request correlation id; quote it in a support request. Logged server-side as `request_id` against the line that explains the failure.

ErrorCode.description: Stable internal domain code, append-only and never repurposed. NOT a closed set: alongside the generic codes below, packages define their own (`coupon_expired`, `insufficient_balance`, `version_not_draft`, `secret_store_unavailable`, `idempotency_key_reused`, and opaque ids such as `auth_001`). Treat an unrecognized code as its HTTP status and show `message`; never fail parsing on it.

FacadeLinkDraft.description: A payment link draft. `draftHash` is also the `ETag`; it covers the product draft the link points at. `link` is null until published.

FacadeLinkDraftProduct.description: What the link draft sells. Either `draftKey` (with its `draftHash`) or `productId`.

FacadeProductDraft.description: A product draft as the public API serves it: the composer's offer with `draftHash` in place of its revision. `draftHash` is also the `ETag`; show it back in `If-Match` to save over or publish exactly this draft. Once published it keeps the hash its approver saw.

customerId.description: The customer's `externalId`, as sent to `customers_create`; not an enrollment id.

productKey.description: The product's natural key, the `key` of its CompanyDocument. Use instead of `productId`.

customerId.description: Enrollment id (product_customers.id) usage is keyed on.

IncludedUnit.description: Public included quantity from the same published product version as the link price. No balance or grant action is implied.

on.description: Existing grant trigger. Cycle grants can precede payment of a renewal.

quantity.description: Included quantity as an exact decimal string.

unit.description: Public display name of the granted unit.

IngestResult.description: Result of an ingestion (single or batch).

aggregation.description: `sum` bills the sum of the events' `value`; `count` bills the number of events, whatever `value` they carry. Anything else is refused with 422 `meter_aggregation_unsupported`.

name.description: Slug `track()` sends against. Immutable once created.

valueProperty.description: Optional and stored as given; billing reads the event's own `value`.

meter.description: The meter this price rates, by slug. Required — a price with no meter is the product's `basePrice`, and two ways to say the same thing lets a product disagree with itself.

tiers.description: Tiers for tiered/volume/package, validated as on createPrice.

InlineProductSpec.description: A product defined inline on a link create, resolved by its natural `key`. A new key creates the product; a known key reuses it, and pricing that differs from the current version publishes a NEW version. That bump is safe because the link created here pins the version it got, so links already in circulation keep selling what they advertised.

basePrice.description: Decimal string. Money never crosses the wire as a float.

billingCycle.description: Required for subscription/prepaid, optional for usage, forbidden for one_time.

key.description: Stable per-tenant natural key. Required — it is what makes creating a link for the same product twice resolve to one product, not two.

meters.description: Meters defined on the product, created once by name. An existing meter is never rewritten: its `name` is the key `track()` ingests against and its `aggregation` decides how past events were counted, so changing either here would retroactively alter what recorded usage meant.

name.description: Display name. Defaults to `key` when omitted.

prices.description: Prices on the version being published, declared in full. A set that differs from what the current version carries publishes a NEW version, the same as a differing `basePrice` — pricing is immutable once published. Omit the field entirely to say nothing about prices; an empty array means "no prices".

status.description: `pending` is a checkout's Order before it is paid (ADR 0004): no number yet, nothing owed until the buyer pays, and it becomes `paid` directly when they do or `void` when the checkout expires. Invoice lists omit it unless `status=pending` is asked for.

successUrl.description: Where the hosted checkout returns after payment.

phone.description: Required before Pagar.me card preparation. Brazilian 10/11-digit national or 55-prefixed number; punctuation allowed.

taxId.description: Optional CPF/CNPJ supplied through the invoice purchase owner before preparation.

consentDigest.description: Required with quoteId and revision for a fresh invoice purchase. Existing financial identities use their original retry protocol.

phone.description: Required for direct Pix. Brazilian 10/11-digit national or 55-prefixed number; punctuation allowed.

taxId.description: CPF (11 digits) or CNPJ (14), punctuation allowed.

InvoiceChargeRequest.description: `CheckoutChargeRequest` on an invoice's own payment page, plus the payer's CPF/CNPJ and phone repairs. Values are stored on the payer only when absent and never replace a different value already on file.

InvoiceId.description: An invoice's id. Starts with `inv_`; the rest is 22 base62 characters. A bare UUID is still accepted as input while clients move over.

InvoicePaidData.description: Body of invoice.paid — the invoice settled. No paymentId: an invoice can settle across more than one payment.

customerId.description: Product enrollment billed. Absent on ad-hoc invoices.

outOfBand.description: True when the merchant marked it paid outside Infi; no payment ran.

payerId.description: Tenant-level customer. Absent on subscription invoices.

reason.description: The merchant's note on an out-of-band settlement.

InvoicePurchase.description: Country and quote state for this purchase, independent of the customer profile.

countryEditable.description: False when a subscription renewal retains its original purchase country.

KeyAccess.description: One key as a person holds it, every grant folded. `past_due` still has access, with a warning. `since` is when the earliest live grant started.

endedReason.description: expired, refunded, charged_back, manual, or subscription_<status>.

until.description: Absent for lifetime or while a subscription keeps it.

LegalSellerView.description: Who sells the Order: the merchant for a direct Brazilian Pix purchase, or the UK Ltd for an eligible merchant-of-record sale. Shown before paying.

LinkAppearance.description: A checkout link's own look: `accentColor` is its button. On a write, an absent field is left alone and "" clears it (inherit again).

LinkCheckoutSession.description: Response to creating/reusing a link checkout session (step 1).

acceptsPayments.description: False when the store cannot receive a payment yet (the UK Ltd has not admitted it): `paymentOptions` is then empty and the checkout says so instead of offering a method. Never omitted.

autoTopupAvailable.description: True when the offer is a credit package (a one-off sale whose product grants credits when paid) and the UK Ltd collects it: the page may offer "automatic top-up", and the charge then takes `autoTopup: true` to save the card under the mandate. Always present.

buyerCountry.description: The stored country; a resumed materialized purchase preserves its original value.

unavailableReason.description: Why this purchase cannot currently accept payment. Missing buyer country allows collecting contact first. Domestic BR card/Pix remains unavailable until Pagar.me dispatch is integrated, without UK fallback. Supplier country can also be missing/conflicting, or the product may still require UK approval (ADR 0026).

LinkCheckoutSessionCoupon.description: What a coupon does to a payment-link purchase, computed server-side. The browser renders these figures; it must not derive a total of its own, because the invoice is priced by the backend at materialization.

code.description: The code as stored — upper-cased and trimmed.

total.description: What the buyer will be charged.

LinkCheckoutSessionState.description: Session read shape — also the `checkout_session.*` webhook payload, which is why it differs from LinkCheckoutSession (`id`, not `sessionId`).

invoiceId.description: Set once the charge step has materialized the invoice.

paymentId.description: Set once a charge has been created.

aggregation.description: Billing sums each event's `value` (a missing value counts as 1, which is what `count` relies on). Only `sum` and `count` can be created; `unique_count`, `max` and `last` appear only on meters created before they were refused, and those bill as a sum.

valueProperty.description: Stored as given; billing does not read it.

recoveryCodes.description: Only for the user's first active device.

MfaDevice.description: Seed-free projection of a registered authenticator.

secret.description: The raw base32 TOTP seed. Shown once; never store it.

MiddlewareError.description: The middleware envelope — nested under `error`, correlation id named `request_id`. Emitted by 429 rate limiting, the Idempotency-Key 409, and a transaction-wrapper 500. A client parsing only the flat Error shape will read no message at all from these.

marginFixed.description: The fixed part of the margin, charged once per paid Order, keyed by ISO 4217 currency, as a decimal string (e.g. `{"USD": "0.50"}`). A currency missing here has no fixed amount decided.

marginPercent.description: Infi's margin as a percentage of the total charged, tax included (ADR 0022), a decimal string. Null until decided.

termsText.description: The terms the digest identifies (Markdown), when the repository holds that text (2026-10-17: the rolling reserve of ADR 0027 and the dispute fee at cost of ADR 0020). Null for a revision whose text is not held.

reason.description: Required to reject; optional note on approve.

sellsOptions.description: The kinds the question offers, allowed ones first.

MorPolicy.description: The product policy in force (ADR 0026) and the version this Account accepted.

NotFoundError.description: 404 body — Error plus the `resource` the lookup was for.

resource.description: Identifier of the missing resource, or an empty string when the handler did not attach one (common — do not depend on it).

error.description: Why it failed; the answer to "why did my customer not get it".

failedAt.description: When the charge first moved to `failed`. Distinct from the provider's own event clock, which later events move.

failureCode.description: Why a failed charge failed, normalized. Never the provider's own message — that stops at the adapter. `superseded` is not a refusal: the buyer abandoned this charge to pay the same invoice another way. Null on a payment that did not fail, and on one that failed before the reason was recorded. Append-only vocabulary: an unrecognized value must render as a generic failure, never break the client.

invoiceUrl.description: PSP hosted payment page. Transient — present only on the create-charge response, not on later reads.

payer.description: Who paid, resolved through the invoice (ad-hoc invoices name a tenant customer directly, subscription invoices name a product enrollment). Present only on the tenant-facing dashboard reads — GET /billing/payments and GET /billing/payments/{paymentID}. Null when the invoice has no resolvable customer.

pixExpiresAt.description: When the pix code expires (pix charges only).

pixPayload.description: Pix copy-paste (EMV/brcode) string, set for pix charges. Render the QR client-side from this. Persisted, so a refresh/poll re-reads it.

pixQrImage.description: Base64 PNG of the pix QR (no data: prefix), returned alongside pixPayload for clients that would rather not render the code themselves.

refundedAmount.description: Total succeeded, non-reversed refunds so far, as a decimal string; absent when nothing was refunded. Partial refunds leave payment status `confirmed`; only a fully refunded aggregate sets `refunded`. Present on tenant-facing reads only.

switchable.description: Whether this charge can still be released so the same invoice can be paid another way (ADR 0026) — true while it is pending, false once it confirmed or failed. Releasing cancels it at the provider where that is supported, and abandons it regardless where it is not. Transient: present on the create-charge response, not on later reads. The hosted checkout keeps the other payment methods clickable while it is true; treat a missing value as false.

customerId.description: Product enrollment billed. Absent on ad-hoc invoices.

payerId.description: Tenant-level customer. Absent on subscription invoices.

PaymentId.description: A payment's id. Starts with `pay_`; the rest is 22 base62 characters. A bare UUID is still accepted as input while clients move over.

PaymentLink.description: A product-bound, reusable, revocable payment link. `token` is a capability, not a credential — anyone holding it can open the checkout, which is the point. It is returned in full on every read because a link is meant to be copied and shared.

cancelUrl.description: Offered to the payer as "back to the merchant" while the checkout is open, and used by the embed as the `?status=error` destination when the charge expires.

productVersionId.description: The product version this link sells, fixed when the link was created. Publishing a new version never reprices a link already issued. Null on links created before pinning existed: those resolve the latest published version at pay time.

successUrl.description: Where the hosted checkout sends the payer after paying, with `?status=success&invoice=…` appended. Stamped onto the invoice the link materializes.

token.description: Opaque public token; the payer URL is /pay/{tenantSlug}/links/{token}.

url.description: The payer-facing address, built server-side. Present so no caller has to re-supply the tenant slug the server already stores in order to learn where to send someone.

billingCycle.description: Billing cycle of the same resolved version as price. Absent for a one-time offer.

description.description: Current public product description, rendered as plain text.

price.description: Version base price as a decimal string. Absent when the version carries none (pure usage pricing).

PaymentLinkView.description: Public display payload for a payment link's landing page.

acceptsPayments.description: False when the store cannot receive a payment yet (the UK Ltd has not admitted it): `paymentOptions` is then empty and the checkout says so instead of offering a method. Never omitted.

autoTopupAvailable.description: True when the offer is a credit package (a one-off sale whose product grants credits when paid) and the UK Ltd collects it: the page may offer "automatic top-up", and the charge then takes `autoTopup: true` to save the card under the mandate. Always present.

cancelUrl.description: Where "back to the merchant" goes, if set on the link.

logoUrl.description: Absent when the merchant has no logo. Absolute, on this API's host (`/pay/{slug}/logo/{file}`), immutable per upload.

successUrl.description: Where the merchant sends the payer after paying, if set on the link.

unavailableReason.description: Why this purchase cannot currently accept payment. Missing buyer country allows collecting contact first. Domestic BR card/Pix remains unavailable until Pagar.me dispatch is integrated, without UK fallback. Supplier country can also be missing/conflicting, or the product may still require UK approval (ADR 0026).

nextCursor.description: Cursor of the next page; null on a short page.

PaymentMethod.description: A credential the payer authorized us to charge again. Display fields only — the provider token, the provider customer reference and the connection are charge material and never appear in an API response.

consentAt.description: When the payer accepted the mandate. Never backfilled or edited — an edited mandate is not evidence in a dispute.

isDefault.description: The credential automatic collection charges. At most one per payer.

status.description: Only `active` is charged. `requires_action` is the cue to ask the customer to update their card (expired, re-branded, mandate revoked); while it is set, automatic collection does not run for that payer. Do not collapse this to a boolean.

PaymentReversedData.description: Body of payment.refunded and payment.chargeback. accessRevoked says whether the buyer's deliverable download grants were cut, so a merchant can mirror the decision in its own entitlements.

PlanChangedData.description: Body of plan.changed — a subscription's plan change took effect. Plans are named by their public key and version, never by id. effectiveAt is when the new plan starts rating the subscription: for an upgrade, the top of the hour it was requested in, announced at once; for any other change, the end of the period it was requested in, announced when that period closes. from is null when the subscription had no plan before (a move off the model before plans, which takes effect at a period boundary like any scheduled change).

buyUrl.description: Path of the public checkout where the buyer can buy more of this balance: /pay/{slug}/links/{token}, the store's active link to a credit package granting this meter. Absent when the store sells none.

consumedLastPeriod.description: Decimal; units debited from this balance in the previous period.

consumedThisPeriod.description: Decimal; units debited from this balance since the current period began.

periodStart.description: When the current period began. Periods are calendar months in UTC.

payUrl.description: Path of the public checkout for this invoice: /pay/{slug}/invoices/{id}.

PortalPaymentMethod.description: A card the buyer keeps at this store; brand, last4 and expiry are absent when the provider did not describe it.

correctedAt.description: When the use was corrected; null if not corrected.

usage.description: What the current period has used so far, per meter. Absent without meters.

amount.description: Decimal; the period's price so far

contentType.description: SVG is refused on purpose: it is a document that runs script when served inline, and the logo route serves inline.

sizeBytes.description: Exact size of the file; signed into the upload URL. At most 1 MiB.

objectKey.description: Echo it back as `logoObjectKey` on `PATCH /account/tenant` once the PUT succeeds.

uploadUrl.description: PUT the file here with the same Content-Type, no auth headers.

currency.description: Optional — defaults to the product's currency.

meterId.description: The meter this price rates. Required and non-null — a price IS a meter rate. A flat recurring amount is not a price: it lives on the version's `basePrice` (ADR 0017 removed meterless prices). Must name a meter on the same product.

tiers.description: Graduated/volume/package tiers, checked with the rules billing rates them by: at least one tier for `tiered`/`volume`/`package`, a positive `size` on a package's first tier, and every amount a decimal string. Anything else is 422 on `tiers`.

flatAmount.description: Decimal string added when the band is used.

size.description: Units per package; package model only.

upTo.description: Inclusive cumulative upper bound, decimal string. Absent or null: the unbounded last band.

accentColor.description: This product's own accent, over the business theme (link > product > business). "" clears it on a write; null inherits.

draftSavedAt.description: The editor's last autosave of an unpublished draft; null when there is none.

guaranteeDays.description: Refund window a portal ask resolves inside on its own.

imageUrl.description: Rendered address of the product photo, served by GET /public/media/{tenantID}/{file}.

ProductCustomer.description:
Product enrollment (product_customers row). The `id` is the enrollment ID
referenced by subscriptions, invoices, usage, and credit wallets.

createsVersion.description: The version publishing would make live; null while the price equals the published one.

publishedVersion.description: What buyers get now; null before the first publish.

savedAt.description: The last autosave; null when nothing is unpublished.

ProductId.description: A product's id. Starts with `prod_`; the rest is 22 base62 characters. A bare UUID is still accepted as input while clients move over.

objectKey.description: An image's key from `POST /catalog/images/presign` (this account's only). Absent on a video.

url.description: A video's https link on a write; on a read, also the image's derived address.

quantity.description: Positive whole quantity of service units.

unitAmount.description: Nonnegative decimal with at most eight fractional places.

valueProperty.description: Optional integration metadata. Metering sums each event's value; this does not extract an arbitrary JSON field.

category.description: Tax category in force; empty when none was set.

taxCode.description: The Stripe Tax code the category maps to.

PublicPagarmeCardPaymentOption.description: Brazilian domestic card. The browser first prepares the purchase, then tokenizes directly with Core v5 using the public key returned by the prepare response. No public key or payer/provider identity is included in the checkout descriptor.

PublicPaymentOption.description: Methods offered for this purchase and buyer country. BR-to-BR Pix uses the merchant's Pagar.me recipient; eligible UK sales use Stripe Elements. Empty when acceptsPayments is false. Charge creation validates again.

PublicPaymentStatus.description: Safe public polling projection. It intentionally excludes PSP references, payer identity, decline details and transient browser-action material.

pixExpiresAt.description: QR presentation deadline; expiry alone does not prove the payment failed.

pixPayload.description: Persisted copy-paste Pix code, available while this payment is pending.

refundedAmount.description: Succeeded, non-reversed refund total as a decimal string.

PublicPixPaymentOption.description: Brazilian purchase collected directly for the merchant's recipient. Repeating charge creation retrieves the same durable Pix attempt.

PublicStripeElementsPaymentOption.description: A sale of the UK Ltd (ADR 0018, amended 2026-10-16): the buyer pays in Stripe Elements on this page, on a Checkout Session of the UK Ltd's account, so nothing is tokenized for Infi. When offered it is the only option; the charge answers with `checkoutAction` to mount.

PublishVersionRequest.description: Optional. Omit the body to publish the ordinary way.

default.description: True (or omitted) makes this the product's default version. False publishes it as an offer, sellable only by a link that names it.

maxPerDay.description: Most top-ups a day. Defaults to 3.

meter.description: A meter the customer's product declares.

quantity.description: Units bought each time (decimal, more than 0).

threshold.description: Buy when the balance falls below this many units (decimal, 0 or more).

meterId.description: Null targets the recurring base fee; that override must use model flat.

ReceivingApplication.description: Exactly one individual or company dossier, plus its bank account. Tenant, actor, provider code, environment and platform account are server-selected. The submitted dossier is immutable in this version.

available.description: BR withdrawable balance; UK approved payout intent net of offsets.

paid.description: Transferred by BR provider; UK lifetime sent beneficiary amount in its actual currency.

pending.description: BR waiting funds; UK unassigned accrued entitlement awaiting release or cycle.

processing.description: Includes provider_unknown; not proof of bank receipt.

receivable.description: Positive debt, negative credit. Kept separate from a future cash forecast.

ReceivingView.description: Provider capabilities from the last applied snapshot, not Infi sale authorization or a guarantee of current provider standing. No dossier, bank data, provider IDs or credentials are returned.

providerId.description: The PSP's own reference for this refund (Stripe's `re_…`). It can be present while an asynchronous refund is still pending.

status.description: A pending row reserves the amount but has no financial effect yet. It stays pending after the provider accepts the refund, until the outcome is confirmed and it becomes succeeded or failed. A succeeded refund can later become reversed.

RefundId.description: A refund's id. Starts with `re_`; the rest is 22 base62 characters. A bare UUID is still accepted as input while clients move over.

SaveLinkDraftRequest.description: Body of `links_save_draft`. `product` names exactly one of `draftKey` and `productId`; `productVersionId` only goes with `productId`.

acceptedTermsVersion.description: The Infi Terms version the operator accepted. Required on live for the first login and must equal `termsVersion` from `POST /auth/session/sync`; sending it is the acceptance. Ignored on sandbox and for a subject already attached.

accountName.description: Display name for the new tenant

signupSource.description: Partner or channel attribution (e.g. lovable, cli, web)

slug.description: URL-safe tenant slug; derived from accountName when omitted

environments.description:
What THIS deployment can say about the caller, and only that: sandbox answers ["sandbox"], live answers ["production"]. Neither computes the union — sandbox cannot read the live database and there is deliberately no cross-deployment call — so a client assembles it by calling the other host, where 403 is the answer "not granted".

Never read from a token claim. Both deployments share one CIAM instance, so a claim travels to both hosts and would BE production access; the grant is a membership row in the database the request landed on.

liveReadiness.description: Whether the primary tenant can actually collect money: the UK Ltd sells for it once it admitted the Account (`GET /account/mor`), so `providerConnected` means admitted and `providers` is `["infi_stripe_uk"]` then. Re-read on every sync. Absent when the state could not be read — a provider lookup must never fail a login.

providers.description: Providers in the `connected` state, the same set charges route on.

mode.description: Which of the two deployments answered, so the dashboard need not be told at build time.

onboardingStep.description: Onboarding is one step — naming the organization. `account` means the session has no tenant yet; `complete` is everything after. The former `product`, `identity` and `integrate` values are gone: the dashboard deleted those screens (frontend ADR 0058).

signupSource.description: Partner or channel attribution stored on the tenant

termsVersion.description: Live only, and only while `needsBootstrap` is true: the Infi Terms version the first live login must accept. Show that version and send it back as `acceptedTermsVersion` on `POST /auth/session/bootstrap`.

cancelReason.description: Why it was, or will be, canceled. Absent when nobody said.

SubscriptionId.description: A subscription's id. Starts with `sub_`; the rest is 22 base62 characters. A bare UUID is still accepted as input while clients move over.

SubscriptionPastDueData.description: Body of subscription.past_due. The subscription became overdue and its first overdue notice was durably requested in the same transaction. This event does not assert that the email was delivered.

TeamRole.description: Fixed merchant role. Only owners manage the team and credentials. Admins perform ordinary business writes; readonly sessions cannot perform business writes. Existing stronger owner and MFA guards remain in effect.

logoUrl.description: The merchant logo the hosted checkout and the embed render next to the merchant name. Absolute, served by `GET /pay/{slug}/logo/{file}`, and immutable per upload (a new upload is a new URL). null when unset; the checkout then shows the merchant's initials.

supportEmail.description: The merchant's contact address: Reply-To on payer-facing email and where Infi sends the merchant's own account notices. null when unset, in which case the owner's login email is used instead.

termsUrl.description: The merchant's terms of use, quoted in the payment mandate a payer accepts before being charged off-session. null when unset.

TopupMeter.description: A meter of the product that can carry a top-up, with what one unit costs.

discountPercent.description: The active plan's permanent top-up discount

cardOnFile.description: The payer has a card saved on a UK account.

minimumPurchase.description: The least a top-up may be worth

pausedReason.description: Why it stopped, e.g. `charge_refused` (the bank refused the card).

quote.description: What one top-up costs now. Null when the unit's price was withdrawn.

UpdateMeterRequest.description: Mutable meter fields; omitted fields are unchanged. `name` is immutable.

aggregation.description: Switching to any other aggregation is refused with 422 `meter_aggregation_unsupported`. A meter created before that refusal keeps its stored aggregation when this field is omitted.

UsageReport.description: Per-meter usage totals for a customer over a window.

ValidationError.description: 422 body. Same flat shape as Error plus `errors[]`, the per-field detail — this array is where the actionable sentence lives (e.g. "product has no published version"), so a client that ignores it discards the fix.

errors.description: Always present on a 422; may be empty.

constraint.description: The rule that failed; currently mirrors `error_code`.

description.description: Customer-safe explanation of this field's problem.

field.description: Request field (JSON name) at fault. Can name a logical input rather than a body key — e.g. `productId` for a path parameter.

value.description: Echoed offending value; empty string when not captured.

isDefault.description: Among a product's published versions, whether this is the one a buyer gets when nothing names a specific version. A published version with `isDefault: false` is an offer reachable only by an explicit pin — a payment link created with `productVersionId` — which is how a product carries a promotional price without it reaching the shelf.

VersionConsumption.description: A version's unit-wallet configuration: which wallet each meter draws, what a unit of that wallet is worth in money, and the gate's floor.

floor.description: Balance below which usage ingestion is refused, as a decimal string. 0 cuts when the wallet empties, a negative value grants that many units of grace, and null never cuts — the deficit is billed as overage at cycle close instead.

VersionConsumptionInput.description: Complete replacement of the version's consumption configuration. An omitted or empty rates/unitPrices array clears it.

floor.description: Decimal string, at most 8 decimal places. Null never cuts.

meter.description: Catalog meter key (e.g. tokens). credits aliases the legacy CRD pool.

total.description: Lifetime credited total for this meter.

idempotencyKey.description: When set, the mutation is idempotent under this key.

reference.description: Free-form reference alias (not deduped). Prefer idempotencyKey.

WalletUnitPrice.description: What one unit of a wallet is worth in money. Used only to turn a cycle-close deficit into an invoice line; absent means the deficit is neither billed nor cleared.

currency.description: 3-letter ISO 4217 code. Defaults to the product's currency.

meterId.description: The meter whose balance is being priced.

unitAmount.description: Positive decimal string, at most 8 decimal places.

events.description: Subscribed event types. Not constrained to WebhookEventType: dispatch matches on `event_type = ANY(events)` with no allowlist, so any event the outbox emits is subscribable. WebhookEventType documents the ones with a described payload.

WebhookEndpointId.description: A webhook endpoint's id. Starts with `we_`; the rest is 22 base62 characters. A bare UUID is still accepted as input while clients move over.

WebhookEventType.description: Event types emitted to the outbox and therefore deliverable to a webhook endpoint. This documents the set with a described payload — it does NOT restrict what an endpoint may subscribe to (see WebhookEndpoint.events), and it is deliberately NOT exhaustive: the outbox also carries payout.*, plan.*, account.* and reconciliation.* families. Each value listed here was verified against its emit site in internal/.

WithdrawalWaiver.description: Present when the charge needs the buyer to waive withdrawal (plan 6f): the page shows `text` beside a box the buyer ticks before paying, and sends `withdrawalWaiver: true`.

bearerAuth.description: A Pulse secret API key presented as `Authorization: Bearer sk_live_...`. Keys are hashed at rest and matched in constant time.

buyerToken.description: A buyer portal token (`bt_...`, ADR 0006): a 30-day session opened by a 6-digit code, or a 1-hour token your server minted with `POST /v1/customer-sessions`. Bound to one store.

publishableKey.description: A browser-safe publishable key (`pk_live_...`) for client-side SDK calls.

receivingWebhookBasic.description: Dedicated webhook username and password for the Brazilian receiving ingress. Dashboard fields were inspected; real authenticated delivery remains an activation gate.

sessionAuth.description: A verified CIAM session token (Clerk JWT) from dashboard login. Requires a linked users row. Pass `X-Tenant-Slug` when the operator belongs to multiple tenants.

get.description: The canonical document: every product that sells with its terms, meters, prices and grants, and the active webhook endpoints. The same document as `GET /config/document`. Secrets are never in it.
get.summary: Pull the account as a company document

post.description: Applies the plan whose `planHash` is in `If-Match`. The body is the same document and options the plan took. If the account moved since the plan, answers 412 `plan_changed` with the plan as it is now and applies nothing. On sandbox it applies (200). On live it only records a proposal (202): the catalog is untouched until a person approves it at `approvalUrl`, also given as `previewUrl`.

202.description: Live proposal; a person approves it at `approvalUrl` (mirrored in `previewUrl`)

post.summary: Apply the plan a caller reviewed

post.description: Diffs the document against the account and answers the plan, in business language (`Accept-Language`: pt-BR or en). `planHash` is the token for `config_apply`, also the `ETag`. Nothing is written, so no `Idempotency-Key`.

For stores with their own login. One hour; the element renews it through your getToken(). `portal:read` (default) never acts; `portal:write` acts without Infi's code, on your responsibility, and needs a key with `billing:write`. A dashboard session or a `pk_` is refused (403 `secret_key_required`). Never creates the customer.
post.summary: Mint a portal token for one of your customers (server side, sk_ only)

post.description: `externalId` revokes every token of that customer. `token` revokes that one `bt_` (the user signed out of the store's login on one device); a dead or foreign token answers `revoked: 0`.
post.summary: Revoke every portal token of one customer, or one token

get.description: For the store's own server, with its `sk_`: the page holds the `bt_` (from the portal's code login or a merchant mint) and the server asks who it is before showing a gated page. `access` lists each product bought and not fully refunded or charged back (`purchase`), and each subscription still running (`subscription`: active, trialing or past_due). A token of another store answers 401 like any invalid one. A GET, so nothing caches it: every call reads the access as it is now.
get.summary: Who a buyer token signs in, and what they have at this store

get.description: The summary always covers the whole account, whatever the page or stage.

post.description:
Enrolls the customer on the product by `externalId`, as `POST /products/{productID}/customers` does: the same `externalId` on the same product is the same enrollment. Name the product by `productId` (`prod_...`) or by `productKey`, the natural key billing as code declares: exactly one of the two, else 422. An unknown `productKey` is a 422 on that field.
The response carries two ids. `enrollmentId` (a uuid) names this customer on this product: the wallet operations and `usage_get` take it. `customerId` (`cus_...`) names the person across products: `customers_get` takes it. `usage_record` takes neither, it takes the `externalId`.

productKey.description: The product's natural key, the `key` of its CompanyDocument. Use instead of `productId`.

enrollmentId.description: The customer on this product: the `enrollmentId` of the wallet operations and `usage_get`.

post.summary: Create a customer on a product

get.description: One meter's balance with `meter`, every balance without it.

parameters.description: Catalog meter key. Omit to list all.
parameters.name: meter

parameters.description: The customer's enrollment id (`enrollmentId` of `customers_create`), a uuid.
parameters.name: enrollmentId

parameters.description: The customer's enrollment id (`enrollmentId` of `customers_create`), a uuid.
parameters.name: enrollmentId

post.description: Increases the customer's balance on the meter. Idempotent when `idempotencyKey` is sent, as `POST /customers/{customerID}/wallet/credit`. A `meter` the enrollment's product does not declare is a 422 on `meter`.

get.description: The read a chat card makes, with `hash`. A different hash answers 412 and the current draft.

put.description: Points at a product draft (`product.draftKey`) or a published product (`product.productId`), exactly one. The return URLs and the look are validated now, as publishing would. `If-Match` follows the rules of `products_save_draft`.

post.description: Publishes the link draft whose `draftHash` is in `If-Match`. When it points at an unpublished product draft, that product is published and the link created in the same transaction: either both happen or neither. The link's hash covers the product's. Returns the link, with its payer `url`.

get.description: Every charge attempt of the account, newest first. Filters run before pagination.
A payment of another account answers 404, as one that never existed.
With `hash`, answers 412 `draft_changed` (and the current draft) when it is not the hash you hold, so a card renders exactly what it showed.

put.description: Saves the complete private composition. Without `If-Match` it only creates: an existing draft answers 412 `draft_changed`. With the `draftHash` you reviewed it updates that draft, or answers 412. The response carries the new `draftHash` and the same value as `ETag`.

post.description: Publishes exactly the draft whose `draftHash` is in `If-Match`. It does not create a link. A repeat with the approved hash answers 200 without publishing again. Records who approved it and `X-Infi-Channel`.

200.description: The published draft, under the approved hash

get.description: Without `from` and `to`, the service's default window applies.

parameters.description: The customer's enrollment id (`enrollmentId` of `customers_create`, a uuid). It is not the `cus_` id of `/v1/customers`.
parameters.name: enrollmentId

get.summary: Get usage totals for a customer

post.description: Same semantics as `POST /metering/events`. Name the product by `productId` or `productKey`: exactly one, else 422. `customerId` is the customer's `externalId` (as sent to `customers_create`), not an enrollment id. `eventId` deduplicates (a replay answers 202 with `duplicate: true`).

202.description: Event accepted, or a replay of one already stored

403.description: Missing scope, or `consumption_blocked`: the customer's balance is exhausted and the product's floor blocks usage. Nothing is recorded.
